rows.speaker: مصعب بن سعد
rows.claim: Musʿab b. Saʿd reports that ʿUthmān responded to reading disputes by collecting written Qurʾan fragments, checking each against the Prophet’s dictation, assigning Saʿīd to dictate and Zayd to write; Ibn Kathīr grades the chain ṣaḥīḥ.
rows.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق، عن مصعب بن سعد قال: قام عثمان فخطب الناس فقال

rows.speaker: كثير بن أفلح
rows.claim: Kathīr b. Aflah reports that ʿUthmān assembled twelve Qurashī and Anṣārī men, including Ubayy and Zayd, and brought the collected sheets; Ibn Kathīr calls this report ṣaḥīḥ.
rows.anchor: عن كثير بن أفلح قال: لما أراد عثمان أن يكتب المصاحف جمع له اثني عشر رجلا

rows.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sīrīn conjectures that the group delayed disputed material so they could identify who had most recently heard the final presentation and write accordingly.
rows.anchor: قال محمد: فظننت ظنا أنما كانوا يؤخرونها لينظروا أحدثهم عهدا بالعرضة الأخيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr clarifies that the collected sheets were with Ḥafṣa; ʿUthmān used them to compile the codex, then returned them to her as promised rather than burning them.
rows.anchor: قلت: الربعة هي الكتب المجتمعة، وكانت عند حفصة، رضي الله عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Ḥafṣa died, Marwān b. al-Ḥakam took and burned the sheets, adopting the rationale ʿUthmān had used for destroying other copies.
rows.anchor: ثم أخذها مروان بن الحكم فحرقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When an explanation is absent from the Qurʾan, Sunna, and Companions, many imams turn to the Successors; Ibn Kathīr names Mujāhid, Saʿīd b. Jubayr, ʿIkrima, ʿAṭāʾ, al-Ḥasan, and others.
rows.anchor: فقد رجع كثير من الأئمة في ذلك إلى أقوال التابعين، كمجاهد بن جبر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says he recited the entire muṣḥaf to Ibn ʿAbbās three times, stopping at every verse to ask its interpretation.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق: حدثنا أبان بن صالح، عن مجاهد، قال: عرضت المصحف على ابن عباس ثلاث عرضات

rows.speaker: ابن أبي مليكة
rows.claim: Ibn Abī Mulayka says he saw Mujāhid ask Ibn ʿAbbās for the Qurʾan’s interpretation with writing tablets; Ibn ʿAbbās told him to write until he had asked about all of it.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي مليكة قال: رأيت مجاهدا سأل ابن عباس عن تفسير القرآن، ومعه ألواحه

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Sufyān al-Thawrī regarded an interpretation transmitted from Mujāhid as sufficient.
rows.anchor: ولهذا كان سفيان الثوري يقول: إذا جاءك التفسير عن مجاهد فحسبك به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Apparent differences in Successor wording often are not real disagreements: one may state an implication or equivalent, while another states the point directly.
rows.anchor: فإن منهم من يعبر عن الشيء بلازمه أو بنظيره، ومنهم من ينص على الشيء بعينه

rows.speaker: شعبة بن الحجاج
rows.claim: Shuʿba b. al-Ḥajjāj and others argue that Successors’ legal opinions are not binding evidence for others, asking how they could be binding in tafsīr.
rows.anchor: وقال شعبة بن الحجاج وغيره: أقوال التابعين في الفروع ليست حجة؟ فكيف تكون حجة في التفسير؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr agrees Successor opinions do not bind those who disagree, but consensus is evidence; where they differ, none overrides another, so consult Qurʾanic usage, Sunna, Arabic usage, and Companions’ views.
rows.anchor: أما إذا أجمعوا على الشيء فلا يرتاب في كونه حجة، فإن اختلفوا فلا يكون بعضهم حجة على بعض

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās attributes to the Prophet a warning that whoever interprets the Qurʾan by opinion or without knowledge should take his seat in the Fire; Ibn Kathīr cites it to prohibit such tafsīr.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " من قال في القرآن برأيه، أو بما لا يعلم

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports that ʿUthmān assigned Zayd, Saʿīd b. al-ʿĀṣ, Ibn al-Zubayr, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. al-Ḥārith to copy codices, directing them to use Quraysh speech if they and Zayd differed in Qurʾanic Arabic.
rows.anchor: عن الزهري: أخبرني أنس بن مالك قال: فأمر عثمان بن عفان زيد بن ثابت وسعيد بن العاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr says al-Bukhārī’s point is that the Qurʾan was revealed in Quraysh’s language, and Quraysh were the foremost branch of the Arabs.
rows.anchor: ومقصود البخاري منه ظاهر، وهو أن القرآن نزل بلغة قريش، وقريش خلاصة العرب

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: ʿUmar reportedly said only Qurashī or Thaqafī youths should dictate in the official codices; Ibn Kathīr grades the chain ṣaḥīḥ.
rows.anchor: عن جابر بن سمرة، قال: سمعت عمر بن الخطاب يقول: لا يملي في مصاحفنا هذه إلا غلمان قريش أو غلمان ثقيف

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Another report says ʿUmar instructed his committee to use the language of Muḍar when linguistic differences arose, because the Qurʾan came in the language of a man from Muḍar, the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قال: إذا اختلفتم في اللغة فاكتبوها بلغة مضر، فإن القرآن نزل بلغة رجل من مضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr cites verses describing the Qurʾan as Arabic and revealed in clear Arabic as evidence for its language, also citing the challenge about a non-Arabic Qurʾan.
rows.anchor: وقد قال الله تعالى: {قرءانا عربيا غير ذي عوج لعلهم يتقون}

rows.speaker: يعلى بن أمية
rows.claim: Yaʿlā b. Umayya wished to witness revelation; when a man in iḥrām wearing perfume and a cloak asked about ʿumra, ʿUmar brought Yaʿlā close to observe the Prophet receive revelation, after which the Prophet ordered the cloak removed and perfume washed away.
rows.anchor: حديث يعلى بن أمية أنه كان يقول: ليتني أرى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين ينزل عليه الوحي

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet’s saying that only two cases merit envy: a person given scripture who recites through the night and a wealthy person who gives charity night and day; al-Bukhārī alone transmits this route, while both Ṣaḥīḥs include a Sufyān route from al-Zuhrī.
rows.anchor: أن عبد الله بن عمر قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: " لا حسد

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet’s parallel saying: one taught the Qurʾan recites it night and day, and one given wealth spends it for the right; neighbors wish they could do likewise.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة؛ " أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "لا حسد إلا في اثنتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger between God and Muḥammad was Gabriel, a noble and honored angel; Ibn Kathīr says God praised both Gabriel and Muḥammad and cites descriptions of them in the Qurʾan.
rows.anchor: أن السفير بين الله وبين محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم جبريل عليه السلام وهو ملك كريم ذو وجاهة وجلالة ومكانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr notes a virtue for Umm Salama, who saw Gabriel, and for the handsome Dihya b. Khalīfa al-Kalbī, whose appearance Gabriel often assumed when visiting the Prophet.
rows.anchor: فضيلة عظيمة لأم سلمة، رضي الله عنها -كما بينه مسلم رحمه الله-لرؤيتها لهذا الملك العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dihya and Usāma b. Zayd were affiliated with Kalb b. Wabara of Quḍāʿa; Quḍāʿa was variously said to descend from ʿAdnān, from Qaḥṭān, or to be an independent branch, and Ibn Kathīr leaves the matter to God.
rows.anchor: وهم قبيلة من قضاعة، وقضاعة قيل: إنهم من عدنان، وقيل: من قحطان

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet saying every prophet received a sign by which people believed, while Muḥammad’s gift was revelation from God; he hopes to have the greatest following on Resurrection Day, and Ibn Kathīr notes its transmission by al-Bukhārī, Muslim, and al-Nasāʾī.
rows.anchor: قال النبي (1) صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ما من الأنبياء نبي إلا أعطي ما مثله آمن عليه البشر

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: A report through Mujāhid and Ibn ʿAbbās says Ubayy b. Kaʿb read the address in 57:13 with alternatives meaning wait for us, delay us, or look toward us.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، عن ابن عباس، عن أبي بن كعب: أنه كان يقرأ: {يوم يقول المنافقون

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: The same report gives Ubayy’s alternatives for the phrase in 2:20 as مروا فيه and سعوا فيه.
rows.anchor: وكان يقرأ: {كلما أضاء لهم مشوا فيه} [البقرة: 20] : "مروا فيه "

rows.speaker: الطحاوي
rows.claim: Al-Ṭaḥāwī and others explain the seven-language allowance as a concession because many people struggled with Quraysh speech, lacking writing, precise notation, and secure memorization.
rows.anchor: قال الطحاوي. وغيره: وإنما كان ذلك رخصة أن يقرأ الناس القرآن على سبع لغات

rows.speaker: الطحاوي والقاضي الباقلاني وأبو عمرو بن عبد البر
rows.claim: Al-Ṭaḥāwī, al-Bāqillānī, and Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr hold that the early concession to recite in seven dialects was later abrogated once hardship ended and memorization, precision, and writing spread.
rows.anchor: وقد ادعى الطحاوي والقاضي الباقلاني والشيخ أبو عمرو بن عبد البر أن ذلك كان رخصة في أول الأمر، ثم نسخ

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view says ʿUthmān consolidated the community on one reading and final recension because variation risked division and mutual accusations of unbelief, then prohibited other readings despite the former concession.
rows.anchor: جمعهم على قراءة واحدة أمير المؤمنين عثمان بن عفان، رضي الله عنه، أحد الخلفاء الراشدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same account compares ʿUthmān’s action with ʿUmar enforcing triple divorce after its repeated use, restricting pilgrimage-season tamattuʿ to keep visits to the Kaʿba from being confined to pilgrimage months, and Abū Mūsā’s obedience in ceasing his fatwa.
rows.anchor: كما ألزم عمر بن الخطاب الناس بالطلاق الثلاثة المجموعة حين تتابعوا فيها وأكثروا منها

rows.speaker: الخطابي
rows.claim: A second view says the Qurʾan’s seven aḥruf do not mean every passage is recited in all seven; different passages may occur in different forms. Al-Khaṭṭābī gives 5:60 and 12:12 as examples.
rows.anchor: كما في قوله: {وعبد الطاغوت}

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says Abū ʿUbayd held this distributed-form view and Ibn ʿAṭiyya selected it; Abū ʿUbayd adds that some dialects fit particular expressions better than others.
rows.anchor: قال القرطبي: ذهب إلى هذا القول أبو عبيد، واختاره ابن عطية. قال أبو عبيد

rows.speaker: القاضي الباقلاني
rows.claim: Al-Bāqillānī says ʿUthmān’s statement that it was revealed in Quraysh speech means most of it, not all: no proof establishes that every word is Qurashī, since Arabic includes all tribes; Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr agrees.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي الباقلاني: ومعنى قول عثمان: إنه نزل بلسان قريش، أي: معظمه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya cites Ibn ʿAbbās, who says he learned فاطر from an Arab describing a well he had begun digging as one he had fathomed or started.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ما كنت أدري ما معنى: {فاطر السماوات والأرض}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr condemns earlier People of the Book for neglecting their scripture in favor of worldly accumulation and urges Muslims to learn, teach, understand, and explain the revelation given to them.
rows.anchor: فذم الله تعالى أهل الكتاب قبلنا بإعراضهم عن كتاب الله إليهم، وإقبالهم على الدنيا وجمعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr links God’s promise to revive dead earth with softening hearts through faith after sin and hardness, citing 57:16–17 as a warning and encouragement to believers.
rows.anchor: كما يحيي الأرض بعد موتها، كذلك يلين القلوب بالإيمان بعد قسوتها من الذنوب والمعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soundest tafsīr method is to explain the Qurʾan by the Qurʾan, then by the Sunna, which clarifies it; al-Shāfiʿī says every ruling of the Prophet was understood from the Qurʾan.
rows.anchor: إن أصح الطرق في ذلك أن يفسر القرآن بالقرآن، فما أجمل في مكان فإنه قد فسر في موضع آخر

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says everything the Messenger ruled was something he had understood from the Qurʾan; Ibn Kathīr supports the method with verses assigning the Prophet the task of explaining revelation.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام أبو عبد الله محمد بن إدريس الشافعي، رحمه الله: كل ما حكم به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says he was given the Qurʾan and something like it along with it; Ibn Kathīr identifies the latter as the Sunna and says the Sunna too comes by revelation, though it is not recited like the Qurʾan.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ألا إني أوتيت القرآن ومثله معه" (1) يعني: السنة

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Zayd b. Thābit recounts that after Yamāma ʿUmar feared the deaths of Qurʾan reciters would erase much of it and persuaded Abū Bakr to collect it; Zayd initially objected that the Prophet had not done so, then gathered it from writing materials and memories. The sheets passed from Abū Bakr to ʿUmar to Ḥafṣa.
rows.anchor: أن زيد بن ثابت قال: أرسل إلي أبو بكر -مقتل أهل اليمامة-فإذا عمر بن الخطاب عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr calls Abū Bakr’s collection one of his greatest deeds, linking it to the divine promise to preserve the Reminder and to the community’s ability to memorize the whole Qurʾan.
rows.anchor: وهذا من أحسن وأجل وأعظم ما فعله الصديق، رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: ʿAlī says Abū Bakr earned the greatest reward for the codices because he was the first to gather the Qurʾan between two covers; Ibn Kathīr grades the chain ṣaḥīḥ.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب، رضي الله عنه، أنه قال: أعظم الناس أجرا في المصاحف أبو بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person may state what he knows about himself when needed, even if others do not know it; Joseph’s claim to be a capable, trustworthy treasurer is the Qurʾanic precedent, and the Prophet’s instruction to learn from four praised the named reciter.
rows.anchor: وهو من إخبار الرجل بما يعلم عن نفسه ما قد يجهله غيره، فيجوز ذلك للحاجة

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: A report from ʿUmar says whoever wants to recite the Qurʾan fresh as revealed should recite in Ibn Umm ʿAbd’s manner; Ibn Kathīr notes routes through Aḥmad, al-Tirmidhī, and al-Nasāʾī, and says al-Dāraquṭnī authenticated it.
rows.anchor: عن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " من أحب أن يقرأ القرآن غضا كما أنزل فليقرأه على حرف ابن أم عبد

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra repeats the instruction to recite as freshly revealed in the reading of Ibn Umm ʿAbd, identified as ʿAbd Allāh b. Masʿūd.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " ومن أحب أن يقرأ القرآن غضا كما أنزل

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports that four Anṣārī Companions had gathered the Qurʾan in the Prophet’s lifetime: Ubayy b. Kaʿb, Muʿādh b. Jabal, Zayd b. Thābit, and Abū Zayd; Muslim also transmits the report.
rows.anchor: سألت أنس بن مالك: من جمع القرآن على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم؟ قال: أربعة

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: A second Anas wording names Abū al-Dardāʾ rather than Ubayy among the four who had gathered the Qurʾan, adding that Anas’s group inherited it.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال: مات النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يجمع القرآن غير أربعة: أبو الدرداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr rejects a literal reading that only these four Companions gathered the Qurʾan: other Muhājirūn certainly did too, so Anas likely meant only the Anṣār; the lists differ over Ubayy versus Abū al-Dardāʾ.
rows.anchor: فهذا الحديث ظاهره أنه لم يجمع القرآن من الصحابة سوى هؤلاء الأربعة فقط، وليس هذا هكذا

rows.speaker: الواقدي
rows.claim: Abū Zayd was otherwise little known, and al-Wāqidī identifies him as Qays b. al-Sakan b. Qays b. Zawʿā b. Ḥarām b. Jundub b. ʿĀmir b. Ghanm b. ʿAdī b. al-Najjār.
rows.anchor: فقال الواقدي: اسمه قيس بن السكن بن قيس بن زعواء بن حرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr says the report was not transmitted only by Ḥamza al-Zayyāt: Ibn Isḥāq also relates it through al-Ḥārith al-Aʿwar; although Ḥamza is weak in hadith, he is an eminent reciter, and criticism of al-Ḥārith concerns belief rather than certain deliberate fabrication.
rows.anchor: لم ينفرد بروايته حمزة بن حبيب الزيات، بل قد رواه محمد بن إسحاق

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr considers the saying more likely to be ʿAlī’s own words than a Prophetic report, which some mistakenly elevated; he calls it sound in meaning and notes a supporting report from Ibn Masʿūd.
rows.anchor: أن يكون من كلام أمير المؤمنين علي، رضي الله عنه، وقد وهم بعضهم في رفعه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ibn Masʿūd and the Prophet calls the Qurʾan God’s banquet, rope, manifest light, beneficial healing, protection, and salvation, and promises ten rewards per letter, counting alif, lām, and mīm separately; Ibn Kathīr calls this route gharīb.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " إن هذا القرآن مأدبة الله تعالى فتعلموا من مأدبته

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم الرازي
rows.claim: Abū Ḥātim calls al-Hijrī weak and not strong, while al-Azdī says he frequently raises reports with many errors; Ibn Kathīr suggests the report may have been mistakenly attributed to the Prophet rather than being Ibn Masʿūd’s saying.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم الرازي: لين ليس بالقوي. وقال أبو الفتح الأزدي: رفاع كثير الوهم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says a person’s state is known by the Qurʾan: whoever loves the Qurʾan loves God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: لا يسأل عبد عن نفسه إلا القرآن، فإن كان يحب القرآن فإنه يحب الله ورسوله

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that a Qurʾan reciter who regularly reviews it resembles someone tending tethered camels: he retains them, but if he releases them they escape; the report is in Muslim and al-Nasāʾī.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " إنما مثل صاحب القرآن كمثل صاحب الإبل المعقلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr corrects Ibn al-Jawzī’s claim that the ʿAbd al-Razzāq route is in both Ṣaḥīḥs: it is unique to Muslim.
rows.anchor: قاله (4) ابن الجوزي في جامع المسانيد، وإنما هو من أفراد مسلم من حديث عبد الرزاق

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports the Prophet’s warning not to say “I forgot such-and-such a verse” but that one was made to forget it; review the Qurʾan, which escapes people’s hearts faster than camels. Al-Tirmidhī grades the report ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
rows.anchor: عن شقيق: سمعت عبد الله قال: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النسائي
rows.claim: Most routes from Manṣūr raise the report to the Prophet, but al-Nasāʾī also transmits it from ʿAbd Allāh as a Companion statement; Ibn Kathīr calls that stopped route unusual.
rows.anchor: وقد رواه النسائي عن قتيبة، عن حماد بن زيد، عن منصور، عن أبي وائل، عن عبد الله موقوفا
